title: The King Who Made His Enemies Carry River Water

lines.text: A king made his enemies carry river water.
lines.caps: a king made his *enemies | carry *river water.

lines.text: All the way from the Ganges, to the Tamil country.
lines.caps: all the way from the *Ganges | to the *Tamil country.

lines.text: His name was Rajendra Chola, son of the builder of Thanjavur.
lines.caps: his name was *Rajendra Chola | son of the builder of *Thanjavur.

lines.text: Around the year ten twenty five, he founded a new capital.
lines.caps: around the year *1025 | he founded a *new capital.

lines.text: He called it Gangaikonda Cholapuram. The city of the Chola who took the Ganga.
lines.caps: *Gangaikonda Cholapuram | the city of the Chola | who took the *Ganga.

lines.text: The temple here was finished in about ten thirty five.
lines.caps: the temple was finished | in about *1035.

lines.text: A royal praise inscription says defeated rulers carried Ganga water, in pots.
lines.caps: a royal inscription says | defeated rulers carried *Ganga water | in *pots.

lines.text: It was poured into a new lake, called Chola Gangam. A victory pillar, made of water.
lines.caps: poured into a new lake | called *Chola Gangam | a victory *pillar | made of *water.

lines.text: Historians note this is the king's own boast. No one else recorded the ceremony.
lines.caps: historians note | it is the king's *own boast | no one else *recorded it.

lines.text: Tradition says its tower was built a little lower, out of respect for his father.
lines.caps: tradition says its tower | was built a little *lower | out of *respect | for his father.

lines.text: Around it, a whole city once stood. Palaces, walls, a fort.
lines.caps: around it a *whole city | once stood | palaces | walls | a *fort.

lines.text: Today, only mounds, brick walls, and broken pillars remain.
lines.caps: today only *mounds | brick walls | and broken *pillars remain.

lines.text: Why the city fell is unclear. Some point to Pandya revenge. Others, to raids from Delhi.
lines.caps: why it fell is *unclear | some say *Pandya revenge | others | raids from *Delhi.

lines.text: Yet the temple survived, and people still worship there.
lines.caps: yet the *temple survived | and people still *worship there.

lines.text: A thousand years on, the king's boast still stands in stone.
lines.caps: a *thousand years on | the king's boast | still stands in *stone.

lines.text: Follow Aazhi for the next chronicle.

sources.title: Gangaikonda Cholapuram (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: capital founded c. 1025 by Rajendra I; temple completed 1035; name meaning; remains (fort wall, palace, mounds); decline causes unclear (Pandya revenge, Delhi raids 1311, 1314, 1327); Ganga-water story as tradition

sources.title: Brihadisvara Temple, Gangaikonda Cholapuram (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: Rajendra I son of Rajaraja I; inscriptions suggest about 1035 (dates debated); tower slightly lower than Thanjavur, respect-for-father is an interpretation; active temple

sources.title: Middle Chola Temples, Gangaikondacholapuram (WisdomLib)
sources.supports: conquered rulers carried Ganga water in pots; new lake called Chola-gangam, a pillar of victory in the form of water, per Tiruvalangadu Plates; ceremony rests on the king's own praise inscription, not independent evidence

illustration: All imagery is an artist's illustration; no portrait of Rajendra Chola survives and none is shown as real; no inscription text is reproduced.
uncertain: Ganga-water ceremony (king's own boast); exact temple date (c. 1020 to 1035 debated); lower-tower-for-respect idea is interpretation; how long the city was capital; reasons for decline; the lion in the well is a later addition so it is not shown as Chola.
pending_second_source: temple tower height not stated in the script because only one source
UNESCO details removed because the UNESCO page could not be fetched
story_device: Journey of the water pots: map of the river road from the Ganges to the Tamil country, a pot carrier's point of view, a lake filling, a tally of pots; ending on ruins at dusk
